title: Almost-sure parity resolvers can depend on transition probabilities
description:
A three-state parity automaton over two letters has two full-support memoryless resolvers that differ at one row. The weighted resolver accepts each fixed input almost surely. The uniform resolver almost surely rejects a fixed input.

The separator records a priority and then independently makes a fresh reset. A weighted transition from the even-priority branch to the odd-priority branch keeps both live masses equal. With uniform weights the even-priority events are summable on a fixed growing-block word, while the odd-priority events recur almost surely. Version 1.0.0 uses four states. This revision retains that proof.

Henzinger, Prakash and Thejaswini posed the fixed-word support question. Baier, Bertrand and Größer’s earlier constructions imply the qualitative separation. The three-state and four-state examples give explicit proofs with just one row changed. Exact replay checks 604 block laws, 2,916 two-block priority pairs and 128 grouped partial sums. The manuscript concerns transition-colored parity and fixed input words. Minimality remains undetermined. Internally reviewed, not peer reviewed.

Under human direction, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the discovery proof and original replay packet. OpenAI Codex reviewed the mathematics and revised the manuscript. GPT-6.2 Sol checked the primary literature, established the transfer from earlier results, and prepared the replay, worked visual and release files. DannyExperiments maintains the repository and is the preferred citation identity. No AI system is proposed as an author.

For the three-state supplement, ChatGPT Astra 6.2 (OpenAI) generated the construction under human direction. OpenAI Codex independently checked the mathematics and block replay. GPT-6.2 Sol checked the scope and literature and prepared the revised manuscript, replay and illustration.
